source_name: MIRRI SR — Ministerstvo investícií, regionálneho rozvoja a informatizácie (Plán obnovy + eurofondy sections)
why_relevant: Managing authority for SK digitalisation money and publisher of the Akčný plán digitálnej transformácie Slovenska 2023-2026 and IROP/Program Slovensko project lists. Names the state actors and programme lines whose procurement then identifies integrators also serving SK banks.

source_name: ITMS2014+ verejná časť (EU funds project & beneficiary register)
why_relevant: Public face of the SK EU-funds monitoring system: implemented projects with signed NFP contracts, beneficiaries, indicators and activities. Gives the beneficiary trail (who received EU money for digitalisation) that pairs with the supplier trail in UVO/TED. Successor system ITMS21+ covers 2021-2027.

source_name: Eurofondy.gov.sk — calls (výzvy) portal for Program Slovensko 2021-2027
why_relevant: Forward-looking view of EU-funded calls; digitalisation calls precede the procurements that name vendors, so this is the earliest reliable signal of upcoming SK IT/financial-infrastructure spend.

source_name: data.gov.sk — open datasets tagged 'eurofondy'
why_relevant: Slovak national open-data catalogue; aggregates machine-readable exports of EU-funds and procurement datasets published by ministries, avoiding fragile scraping of ITMS/UVO front-ends.

source_name: EU Cohesion Open Data Platform
why_relevant: Commission-run platform with ESIF/cohesion allocations, spend and beneficiary datasets per member state, including Slovakia. EN-language, structured, and comparable across countries — useful for sizing SK digitalisation envelopes that feed banking-adjacent IT projects.

source_name: Opentender.eu — Slovakia portal (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Re-publishes TED plus the SK national portal (ÚVO) as cleaned, structured contracting data covering 35 jurisdictions, including below-threshold SK contracts. Fastest route to supplier-level aggregation and market-share style views without building the ETL ourselves; also carries integrity indicators.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP)
why_relevant: Where EBRD clients post procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract-award notices for EBRD-financed contracts. Award notices name suppliers — the IFI-side equivalent of TED awards for banking/fintech modernisation projects.

source_name: EBRD — Slovak Republic country page and project/news feed
why_relevant: Country-level record of EBRD activity in SK, and the EBRD Digital Approach frames which financial-sector digitalisation projects get funded. Project summary documents typically name the client financial institution and the scope, from which technology partners can be inferred or followed up.

source_name: EBRD corporate procurement (SMART by GEP)
why_relevant: EBRD's own supplier-facing platform for goods/works/consultancy. Relevant secondarily: consultancy assignments on SK financial-sector reform are contracted here, and consultant identities reveal advisory competitors in the region.

source_name: EIB — Financed projects database (loans) and pipeline
why_relevant: Searchable register of EIB-financed and pipeline projects with country filter; SK entries include intermediated credit lines through commercial banks, naming the financial intermediary. Establishes which SK banks carry EU-backed programmes — a partnership and account-mapping signal.

source_name: EIF — Slovakia country page and guarantee-deal news
why_relevant: EIF publishes each InvestEU/EFSI guarantee signed with a named SK financial intermediary (SZRB, ČSOB, Komerční banka for CZ+SK, etc.), with volumes and expected beneficiary counts. Directly identifies which SK banks are running EU-backed lending products — a strong partnership and product-roadmap indicator.

source_name: Slovak Investment Holding (SIH) / SZRB — fund-of-funds financial instruments
why_relevant: SIH, 100% owned by SZRB, manages over EUR 1bn of EU shared-management instruments and channels them through commercial banks. Its disclosures and the fi-compass case study reveal which SK financial institutions act as intermediaries and what systems/reporting obligations they must support.

source_name: European Commission — Investment Plan for Europe: Slovakia results page
why_relevant: Consolidated EFSI scoreboard for SK: counts of EIB projects and EIF agreements with intermediary banks/funds and mobilised investment. Useful as a cross-check and as a pointer into the underlying EIB/EIF deal records.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — international financial institutions (EIB/EBRD relations)
why_relevant: SK Ministry of Finance is the shareholder-side counterpart for EIB/EBRD and states that EIB projects in SK are published; a stable pointer to official SK positions, guarantees and which state entities borrow.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA)
why_relevant: Central register of EU-institution grants and tenders plus funded project records (participants, coordinators, budgets). Captures SK financial-sector participants in EU programmes (e.g. digital/cyber calls) that never appear in national procurement.

source_name: Partnerská dohoda / ÚVO institutional page (EU-funds procurement rules for SK)
why_relevant: Explains how ÚVO oversees procurement of EU-funded contracts in SK and links the ITMS/partnership-agreement machinery to the procurement bulletin — the connective tissue between the funding trail and the vendor trail.

source_name: EURACTIV.sk — digitalisation section (state IT procurement scrutiny)
why_relevant: SK-language journalism that scrutinises large state IT tenders (e.g. a EUR 68m system criticised by experts), often naming bidders, prices and controversies that procurement notices state neutrally. Useful for context, controversy flags and vendor-reputation signals.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Slovakia and TED publications
why_relevant: Registry entries describe exactly what SK and TED contracting datasets contain, their coverage, format and download endpoints — the fastest way to choose a stable ingestion path instead of guessing at portal exports.

source_name: NBS Register podľa PSD2 (PSD2 register of payment service providers)
why_relevant: Statutory PSD2 register naming every SK-licensed/registered payment service provider with per-service records (AISP, PISP, PIISP) and activity start/end dates. This is the definitive competitor universe for SK payments and the anchor for A6 vendor/competitor mapping.

source_name: NBS subjekty.nbs.sk PSD2 JSON API
why_relevant: Machine-readable daily-refreshed JSON of PSD2 institutions: business name, address, ID number, PSD2 service types and activity dates. Directly ingestible as the structured backbone of an SK payments competitor register; documented by NBS itself as synchronised by 05:00 CET daily.

source_name: NBS subjekty finančného trhu — supervised entities database
source_subtype: regulatory entity database with bulk export
why_relevant: Master searchable database of all NBS-supervised entities across nine sectors, including 'banky, platobné služby a elektronické peniaze' and 'trh s kryptoaktívami'. Offers a 'Databáza na stiahnutie' bulk download. Broadest single actor list for the SK banking+payments competitor universe.

source_name: NBS Platobné inštitúcie a AISP (supervision section)
why_relevant: Supervision landing page for PI/AISP: licensing conditions, business requirements, EEA passporting notifications. Explains the licence categories that structure the competitor register and signals which foreign PSPs may passport into SK.

source_name: NBS Podmienka L — outsourcing and external ICT-risk description in PI licence applications
why_relevant: Spells out that PI licence applicants must describe agents, outsourced activities and contractual arrangements with external ICT service providers. This is the regulator-mandated disclosure logic that makes vendor relationships (processors, card personalisation, hosting, core-payment platforms) discoverable — the highest-value A6 vendor lead on the regulator side.

source_name: NBS Digitálna prevádzková odolnosť finančného sektora (DORA) hub
why_relevant: NBS DORA hub covering the register of information on ICT third-party contractual arrangements (mandatory from 17.1.2025), ICT incident reporting and DORA legislation. The register-of-information reporting cycle is the single most systematic regulator-side mapping of which ICT vendors serve which SK financial institutions.

source_name: NBS Výroky právoplatných rozhodnutí + Archív rozhodnutí (enforcement and licensing decisions)
why_relevant: Published operative parts of final NBS decisions — licence grants, withdrawals, sanctions, prior-consent approvals for qualifying holdings. Reveals ownership changes, market entries/exits and compliance failures among SK payment and banking actors; the archive gives historical depth.

source_name: Vestník NBS (official bulletin, by year)
why_relevant: Official gazette carrying NBS decisions, opatrenia and methodological guidance, e.g. rozhodnutie NBS č. 10/2022 on SEPA payment service provider rules. Authoritative primary text for the rules that shape SK payment-market structure and reporting obligations.

source_name: NBS Oversight — Systémy spadajúce pod oversight NBS
why_relevant: Names the payment systems, schemes and arrangements that fall under NBS oversight. Identifies the infrastructure operators (and, indirectly, their technology suppliers) that sit under SK retail and large-value payments.

source_name: NBS Oversight — Regulácia a pracovné rámce (PFMI, SIPS Regulation, PISA, CROE)
why_relevant: Sets out the frameworks NBS applies: CPSS-IOSCO PFMIs, ECB SIPS Regulation (EU) 2025/1355, the retail payment systems framework, the PISA framework for payment instruments/schemes/arrangements and CROE cyber-resilience expectations. Defines the assessment criteria against which SK payment infrastructures and schemes are judged — useful for anticipating vendor/compliance demand.
